definitions.explanation: A graded level in a system of ranking — used for beef, wine, hotel rooms, paychecks, insurance, and judo/karate. Implies an ordered scale with clear criteria, distinguishing top grades from lower ones.

examples.japanese: {肉|にく}の{等級|とうきゅう}を{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: To check the grade of the meat.

examples.japanese: {自動車|じどうしゃ}{保険|ほけん}の{等級|とうきゅう}が{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: My car insurance rating went up (a grade).

examples.japanese: {和牛|わぎゅう}は{脂肪|しぼう}の{入|はい}り{方|かた}で{等級|とうきゅう}が{細|こま}かく{分|わ}かれている。
examples.english: Wagyu beef is finely graded based on the marbling of the fat.

notes:
Compound of {等|とう} (class) + {級|きゅう} (grade). The reading is とうきゅう (be careful: the homophone {投球|とうきゅう} means "pitching").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {等級|とうきゅう}が{上|あ}がる/{下|さ}がる: a grade goes up/down
- {等級|とうきゅう}{分|わ}け: classifying by grade
- {最高|さいこう}{等級|とうきゅう}: the highest grade
- {等級|とうきゅう}{制度|せいど}: grading system
- A5{等級|とうきゅう}: A5 grade (top wagyu grade)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {格付|かくづ}け: rating; ranking — emphasizes the act of evaluating
- ランク: rank — borrowed from English; more casual
- {級|きゅう}: grade (single character) — used in martial arts and tests ({1|いっ}{級|きゅう}, {2|に}{級|きゅう})
- {階級|かいきゅう}: class; rank — military or social class
